answer: An agent economy can require a refundable stake before an identity may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud, such as collusion or fabricated results. This does not prove that one account equals one person; it makes multiplying accounts costly: every sybil ties up capital, and detected abuse destroys part of it. A zephyr job may be cheap, but a dune of fake identities still needs separate stakes, while shale-like collateral is locked until review ends.
